description: Slices the source into segments of segdur seconds and plays each segment repets times before moving on - the stuck-vinyl / skipped-CD effect. Source-verified mechanics (extend/iterate.c do_doubling): each written repetition is segdur minus a fixed 5 ms crossfade splice, and the FINAL segment - partial or even exactly full - is silently dropped, so the output is repets * (segdur - 0.005) * floor-count-of-full-segments. The duration model reproduces this sample-exactly on all seven probe runs (segdur 0.1-0.5, repets 2-4, 1 s and 2 s inputs; worst error 0.012%). Works on mono and stereo input.
musical_use: The needle stuck in the groove: with speech or conventional music a short passage repeats for emphasis; with complex material it becomes a pulsing, mechanical throb. Long segments (0.5 s+) read as clear loops; short segments (tens of ms) give sputtering, glitchy, locked-groove repetition. segdur takes a breakpoint file, so the slice length can evolve over the file - sweep from micro-stutter up to phrase-length loops in one pass, a classic gesture. Also useful simply to extend material before further transformation. Each repetition loses 5 ms to the splice, so very short segdur values shrink the output audibly and soften transients; the sync flag instead skips ahead in the source so the output tracks the input timeline (approximately) rather than multiplying it.

segdur.description: Duration of each slice (CDP-enforced 0.01 s to the input duration: 3.0 on a 2 s file refused with 'Value (3.000000) out of range (0.010000 to 2.000000)' - the maximum is input-dependent). Each written repetition is segdur minus the fixed 5 ms splice. Breakpoint-capable, banner-confirmed ('can vary through time'): a 0.1-to-0.4 envelope exits 0 and differs from both endpoint scalar renders; the envelope's time axis tracks the INPUT approximately (it advances by segdur - 0.005 per consumed segment). WARNING: segdur equal to the full input duration is accepted but produces a ZERO-frame output (see known_issues).

repets.description: Number of times each segment is played, including the first pass (CDP-enforced range 2-32: 1 refused with 'Parameter[2] Value (1.000000) out of range (2.000000 to 32.000000)'); the output is roughly repets times the input length. Scalar only - a breakpoint file is refused.

sync.description: Outfile tries to stay synchronised to the infile: after writing the repeats, reading skips ahead in the source, so the output no longer multiplies the duration (verified 2.2049 s from a 2 s input at segdur 0.25 / repets 3 - near the input length, not exactly it). The duration model above assumes this flag is OFF and will over-predict when it is on. Engine limitation: validate_params rejects bool true/false values, so pass the number 1 to enable; omit the parameter entirely to disable (any supplied value, even 0, switches the flag on).

examples.description: Locked-groove loop: quarter-second slices, each played three times.
examples.expected_use: A 2 s source yields 21 x 0.245 s = 5.145 s (sample-exact); vinyl-stuck repetition of each quarter second.

examples.description: Stutter-to-loop sweep: slice length grows from 50 ms to 0.5 s across the source.
examples.expected_use: Glitchy micro-repeats opening out into phrase loops; duration not pre-predictable with a breakpointed segdur (pre-flight skips).

known_issues: FINAL SEGMENT SILENTLY DROPPED (source-confirmed): the last segment - including the boundary case where the input is an exact multiple of segdur - is never written. Extreme case: segdur equal to the input duration (the allowed maximum) exits 0 with a ZERO-frame output file plus 'WARNING: Can't close output sf-soundfile : can't truncate SFfile'. Keep segdur well below the input duration.

Duration-model edge: the floor term uses (indur - 0.0001), so if the input exceeds an exact multiple of segdur by less than 0.1 ms the model under-predicts by one segment block (up to repets * segdur seconds). Everywhere else the model is sample-exact (worst observed 0.012%).
Every repetition is 5 ms shorter than segdur (fixed SPLICEDUR crossfade, 221 samples at 44.1 kHz); at segdur 0.01 (the minimum) half of each slice is splice.
The sync flag changes the duration semantics entirely (output tracks the input length approximately); the duration model assumes it is off.
repets breakpoint refusal: 'ERROR: Cannot read parameter 2 [b3_rp.brk]: brkpnt_files not permitted.'
Inputs shorter than 10 ms are refused outright ('Input file is too short for this process.', source: doublets_preprocess).
